Systematic Reviews and Other Evidence Synthesis. # Systematic Reviews and Other Evidence Synthesis. * What is a Systematic Review? * Steps in a Systematic Review. **Systematic reviews and scoping reviews should have a protocol which helps to plan and outline the study methodology. * Many journals now require submitted systematic reviews to have registered protocols. * The PRISMA Reporting Standard lists information about the systematic review protocol as an "essential element" (PRISMA 2020 Item 24). * The Cochrane Handbook, The Institute of Medicine Standards, and others, all list completing a protocol as one of the important steps to a successful systematic review. * Best practices in systematic reviews: the importance of protocols & registration. * PRISMA for systematic review protocols (PRISMA-P). Checklist and explanation of what should be included in a systematic review protocol. * The PROSPERO systematic review protocol template. * JBI scoping review protocol template. * Generalized Systematic Review Registration Form. These resources will help authors prepare a protocol for a systematic or scoping review. * JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis - Section 1.3 (Systematic reviews) & 11.2 (Scoping reviews). After you write the protocol, you should register it with a review registry. Registration is free and open to anyone undertaking systematic reviews. Some journals also publish systematic review protocols. * PROSPERO - International Register of prospective Systematic reviews. PROSPERO is an international database of prospectively registered systematic reviews in health and social care. Key features from the review protocol are recorded and maintained as a permanent record in PROSPERO. This will provide a comprehensive listing of systematic reviews registered at inception, and enable comparison of reported review findings with what was planned in the protocol. OSF can be used to pre-register a systematic or scoping review protocol and to share documents such as a citation management library, search strategies, and data extraction forms. Unlike other registries, evidence synthesis author teams do not submit their protocols for review by an editorial board before they are accepted and pre-registered on OSF. Otherwise, protocols are peer reviewed. Like systematic reviews, scoping review protocols can be published in some journals. This open access title publishes protocols of systematic reviews broadly related to health sciences.

results.title: How to register a Systematic Review Protocol in PROSPERO | CW Authors
results.content: # Basics of Registering your Protocol for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses. # **Basics of Registering your Protocol for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses**. In terms of transparent and unbiased research, it can be argued that registration of your protocol is **as important as it is as for clinical trials**, because systematic reviews and meta-analyses are often used for decision-making in fields like healthcare. The other main purpose of registering your protocol is for other researchers in your field, or similar fields, to be notified when a study such as yours is being conducted. In return for using this service for free, authors are expected to be accountable to the **standards** they set in their protocols. Prospectively submitting your systematic review or meta-analysis protocol is a positive step to take, holding you and your colleagues accountable for the quality of your work and helping to foster a culture of transparency in academic research.

results.title: What is PROSPERO and why you should register your systematic review with it: Read here 👇 https://lnkd.in/d9QjXCvZ | Mushtaq Bilal, PhD
results.content: What is PROSPERO and why you should register your systematic review with it: PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews) is an online database of systematic review protocols. Registering your systematic review prospectively (i.e. before you start conducting your review) helps you keep your review process transparent and reduce the risk of bias, which in turn lead to increased credibility of your research. Prospectively registering your systematic review with PROSPERO also helps you with publication of your review. results.title: Writing a protocol for clinical research | Simbec-Orion
results.content: A clinical research protocol is one of the most vital components of any study. ## **What is a clinical research protocol?**. A clinical research protocol is a document that outlines how a clinical trial will be conducted and the clinical trial management processes that will be in place throughout the study. As well as outlining the study plan, the research protocol also describes the safeguarding and safety measures that the study will follow. The main purpose of the research protocol is to outline the study plan, with guidelines for the research to follow. As such, the guidelines provided in the study protocol ensure that the trial stays centred around the main aims and objectives of the research. The background section will also provide a statement regarding how the trial will be conducted in compliance with the protocol; as well as Good Clinical Practice and any other regulatory standards. The study design section provides a detailed description of the trial design, including how the trial will be conducted in order to meet the primary and secondary endpoints of the research. In order to attain a well-defined population, the clinical research protocol outlines subject inclusion and exclusion criteria. Efficacy and safety are split into two sections in the clinical study protocol. This section of the study protocol should also cover the procedures for assessing, reporting and analysing efficacy throughout the trial. This section of the research protocol provides a description of the statistical methods used in the study. This section of the research protocol outlines the quality control measures that will be put into place throughout the study. The research protocol should state ethical considerations of the study in line with Good Clinical Practice regulations, as well as any local regulations or laws. Similarly, the study protocol’s ethical section should state the responsibility of the investigator to obtain signed informed consent from subjects prior to participation in the trial. The clinical research protocol should end with an appendices section. From study background, trial design, ethical considerations and key definitions, it’s important to provide a comprehensive overview of the research, and provide specific guidelines on study procedures.
